overview.text: ZCG announced on 26 May that the Security & Vulnerability Disclosure Initiative and its bounty were closed with immediate effect. It argued that AI-assisted tools make submissions cheap to produce, so duplicate and speculative reports were absorbing scarce engineering attention, pointing to curl's experience. Responsible disclosure stays open, Least Authority's audit work continues, and ZCG is working with Zellic on V12 access.

scalar, shieldedonly and earthrise disputed closure as the remedy. scalar called it a design flaw that turns a filtering problem into the loss of a security channel and urged moving to HackerOne, Immunefi or HackenProof; shieldedonly replied that a critical report of his sat untriaged on HackerOne for three weeks and argued for AI-assisted triage; earthrise proposed a narrower bounty for severe bug classes that requires proof of exploit on testnet. artkor, for ZCG, agreed the program could not continue in its current form but said valid findings would not be overlooked.

A separate strand involved ouicate, whose posts in this stretch are deleted or missing from the data. artkor wrote a hypothetical about a reporter who feels brushed off (#7), then posted an instruction aimed at an AI and said the other party had programmed an AI bot too rigidly (#11, #13); scalar posted a proof-of-work challenge presented as a submission rule (#16, #26). daira of ZODL said ZODL had not brushed off reporters and its assessments were never tied to ZCG's payout categories (#22), and that the remediation team does not submit payout requests to ZCG (#23).

From June most posts concern payment. artkor said final verification was underway and that the Zebra reports would be announced first, other repositories later (#47, #51), and FPF confirmed a payout (#52). Reporters asked whether pre-launch Zebra reports would count (#53, #59). On GHSA-pvmv-cwg8-v6c8, ZcashFoundation explained that the reward goes to the earlier of two independent reports and admitted it had omitted the GHSA from its report to ZCG (#67); fivelittleducks asked for a discretionary partial payout for the duplicate (#69).

Through July and September, reporters including fivelittleducks, ipwning, haxonittech, Prince and Alen repeatedly asked for status and timelines. artkor said he would stop answering ouicate's private messages (#79) and daira said there was no bandwidth until after NU6.3 activation (#82). On August 25 zerodartz gave the first substantive update: a third-party reviewer had delivered most GHSA details, core developers had been stretched thin, and all eligible bounties would be paid.

In October payment messages began reaching reporters (#108); ZCG said it contacts reporters only through the contact details they supplied and corrected itself after confusing two reporters named Prince (#109, #111). ouicate congratulated those who were paid (#121). shieldedonly asked whether his pre-launch Zebra reports could be rewarded and was pointed to the Q4 coinholder call for proposals (#115 to #117, #120), and coms asked about CVE numbers for post-closure reports (#123).

positions.label: Close the bounty; keep disclosure open and audit work going
positions.summary: AI tools have made reports cheap to produce, so the bounty drew a growing volume of duplicate, low-signal and speculative submissions whose human triage pulled scarce attention from remediation, audits and releases. Closing it while keeping responsible disclosure, Least Authority's work and AI-assisted auditing is the sustainable path, and valid findings will not be overlooked.

positions.label: Keep the bounty but fix filtering and triage
positions.summary: Closure turns a filtering problem into the loss of an invaluable security channel, and unrewarded disclosure pushes researchers toward exploits or rival programs. The remedy is strict rules, clear PoC requirements and automated or AI-assisted triage, or moving to an established platform, though shieldedonly reports that platforms have triage delays of their own.

positions.label: Narrow the bounty to severe bug classes with proof of exploit
positions.summary: Limit rewards to the most severe classes (inflation, chainsplits, zcashd RCE) and require the reporter to demonstrate the exploit on testnet, so engineers know a serious bug exists before reading the report. earthrise lists the downsides: extra testnet work and possible leakage, mitigated by private testnets.

positions.label: Engineering teams assess for their own use; payout rules were ZCG's
positions.summary: ZODL says it has not brushed off reporters and its assessments mainly prioritize its own mitigations, never promised to match ZCG's payout categories, and it does not submit payout requests for researchers. zancas says he had no input into the program and that a Zaino DoS needing a malicious validator may not qualify.

positions.label: Payouts follow program terms and a staged review; be patient
positions.summary: ZCG and Foundation voices say the review proceeds in stages with Zebra first, pending reports cannot be discussed, and duplicates follow the first actionable disclosure. artkor adds that Zcash is decentralized and procedure matters less than impact; zerodartz says a third-party reviewer is finalizing GHSA details and all eligible bounties will be paid.

positions.label: Reporters want payouts, status updates and recognition for pre-launch work
positions.summary: Reporters with accepted or credited advisories say they have had no payout instructions or timeline for weeks to months, ask for clarity on who decides and when, ask whether pre-launch Zebra reports and independent duplicates can be rewarded, at least with an appreciation payment, and ask for a timeline for lightwalletd, Zaino and zcashd reports.

summary.tldr: ZCG closed its vulnerability bounty, citing a flood of duplicate and AI-generated reports; critics wanted better triage or a platform instead. Most of the thread then became reporters asking about delayed payouts, with ZCG saying review was staged and, by late August, that eligible bounties would be paid.
